summary.headline: KP Green H1 FY27 total income up 27% to ₹682 crore, but PAT fell to ~₹32 crore from ₹58 crore; order book ₹1,892 crore.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 total income rose 27% YoY to ₹682 crore and EBITDA grew 17% to ₹119 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 17.4% and profit after tax fell to about ₹32 crore from ₹58 crore as depreciation and interest rose with new capacity. Management guided H2 EBITDA margin of 5-7%, citing raw material (zinc, gas) cost pressure from geopolitical issues, and guided FY27 revenue of about ₹1,800 crore. Order book closed September at ₹1,892 crore after about ₹770 crore of new orders in the half. Capacity utilisation was stated at 40-50%, with a target of about 70% by year end. Management also announced a statutory auditor change to BDO and a promoter equity infusion of about ₹100 crore.

segments.name: Galvanizing
segments.commentary: Asia's largest galvanizing facility with 19,000 tpa capacity and a 15-ton single dip; utilisation ramped from 35-40% to about 50%, with a target of 70% by year end. Zinc and gas cost increases have hit costing.

segments.name: Related-party (KP group) orders
segments.commentary: Management said related-party orders were about 17% of sales in the period versus about 50% last year, and that the company wants more external orders.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at about ₹1,800 crore, implying H2 revenue growth of around 30% YoY; ₹1,000-1,200 crore of this is expected from the related-party group per the analyst's summary, which management confirmed.
EBITDA margin guided at 5-7% for the next two quarters; management said it cannot predict raw material prices.
Capacity utilisation expected to reach about 70% next year, with H2 utilisation expected to be higher than H1.
Order book expected to exceed ₹2,500 crore by mid-next year (around mid-FY28).
Around ₹300 crore of capex planned over the next 18 months; depreciation in H2 expected to be similar to H1.
Management aims for about 25% revenue CAGR over the next five years, while acknowledging it may be over-optimistic.
capex_capacity: Total manufacturing capacity about 4 lakh tonnes; facility spans about 55 acres.
Galvanizing capacity 19,000 tpa; ramp-up from 35-40% to about 50% utilisation, target 70% by year end.

Planned new products: hot-rolled mill (to reduce raw material purchases from the market) and offshore tubular/hybrid lattice towers for 5.4 MW wind turbines; land already purchased, with commencement targeted in the next financial year.
Around ₹300 crore of capex planned over the next 18 months, per management.
demand_pricing: Order book ₹1,892 crore at end-September, with about 9-10 months of current revenue run rate covered; management targets 12-15 months of cover.
New orders in H1: about ₹240 crore in July, ₹458 crore in August and ₹270 crore in October (partly after period end).
BSNL 4G saturation project order of about ₹819 crore covering supply and erection at about 1,280 sites.
Management cites India's pre-engineered building market growing from about ₹21,000 crore to about ₹38,900 crore by 2030; transmission investment of about ₹9 lakh crore over 2023-2032.
Margins: management claims 17% EBITDA margin is best in class versus peers at 12-14%, and says H2 margin will remain at 5-7% because of raw material cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Why has related-party share of sales fallen to about 17% from 50%, and what is the order book pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no slowdown at the KP group; the company is shifting to external orders, with larger BSNL orders (~₹800 crore). Order book is expected to exceed ₹2,500 crore by next mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital stressed and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher receivables from BSNL orders (payment retention) and lower payables due to growth; management expects operating cash flow to turn positive after March (FY28).

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth below expectations if capacity is idle, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality, rain-related slowdowns, geopolitical issues and raw material price volatility; utilisation is 40-50% and it expects about 70% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will galvanizing ramp-up and H2 growth of 30% with normal margins be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Galvanizing utilisation moved from 35-40% to about 50%, with 70% targeted by year end. Revenue guidance is about ₹1,800 crore for FY27, but margins are guided at 5-7% for the next two quarters; zinc and gas costs have been the reason.

qa_highlights.question: Will depreciation and interest in H2 be similar to H1, and what drives the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said depreciation in H2 will be broadly similar to H1 (about ₹28 crore) and that H2 margin is guided at 5-7%, which it considers conservative.

qa_highlights.question: How will the planned growth and capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter committed about ₹100 crore equity infusion: ₹25 crore in the next 30-60 days and ₹75 crore within 18 months. Management also said further debt and equity would be needed.

risks_watch: Profit after tax fell about 45% YoY despite revenue growth, driven by depreciation and interest from new capacity; H2 depreciation and interest are expected to stay at similar levels.
Zinc and natural gas cost increases linked to geopolitical issues are compressing margins; management cannot predict raw material prices.
Working capital stress: receivables are rising from BSNL retention, and operating cash flow is not expected to turn positive until after March.
Debt has risen to ₹447 crore from ₹196 crore, with debt-to-equity at 0.91x, and the company plans about ₹300 crore of capex over 18 months.
Watch whether utilisation reaches the targeted 70% and whether the order book rises to ₹2,500 crore by mid-FY28.
Auditor change to BDO and related-party revenue mix shift are items to monitor.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and order book visibility, but cautious and conservative on near-term margins, which management guided at 5-7% and attributed to raw material volatility. Responses on depreciation, working capital and H2 growth were less precise and mostly deferred to later guidance.
key_quotes: So we would still like to be more outward driven and have less interrelated party orders.
The margin as I just explained considering the issues around will be in the range of five to seven percent and they still remain best in class compared to our competitors.
We are not saying that there will be like we can predict about the raw material price.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Order book to exceed ₹2,500 crore by mid-FY28

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book and long-term growth but cautious on near-term margins (guided 5-7% for H2) and vague on depreciation, working capital and H2 growth; analysts pushed on falling PAT, idle capacity and cash flow.
